intended_object: The canonical isomorphism sheafify(P) ⋙ F ≅ sheafify(P ⋙ F), for a functor F that preserves the multiequalizers and cover-indexed colimits used by the plus construction (here sheafification is P⁺⁺). Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: J.sheafify P is defined as P⁺⁺. The body composes two isomorphisms. First, plusCompIso applied to P⁺ gives (P⁺)⁺ ⋙ F ≅ (P⁺ ⋙ F)⁺. Second, plusFunctor applied to plusCompIso F P gives (P⁺ ⋙ F)⁺ ≅ (P ⋙ F)⁺⁺. Together they give the stated isomorphism. Lemmas in the same file show it is compatible with the unit toSheafify and equals the map from the universal property, so it is the canonical isomorphism. The hypotheses are exactly those the plus construction needs in D and E, plus F preserving the relevant limits and colimits; the definition is about the concrete plus-plus sheafification, so its content needs this setting. The abstract version, CategoryTheory.sheafifyComposeIso (stated in the opposite direction, under PreservesSheafification), exists separately and is linked to this one by a lemma. Nothing is wrong and it is not too narrow.
